name: Elemental Plane
summary: Across the Elemental Plane, its wards still hold the elementals—though cracks now let them reach Azeroth. The titans made this realm to imprison Azeroth’s chaotic elementals, dividing it into Skywall, Deepholm, the Abyssal Maw, and the Firelands. Breaches have brought violent incursions and catastrophic summonings into Azeroth.

sections.title: A Prison for Primordial Chaos
sections.body: Long ago, the elementals served as lieutenants to the Old Gods. The titans defeated the Old Gods, then banished the elemental lords and their many servants to the Elemental Plane. They divided the realm into four domains: Skywall for air, Deepholm for earth, the Abyssal Maw for water, and the Firelands for fire. With the elementals gone, nature calmed and peace returned to Azeroth’s surface.

sections.title: Endless Strife
sections.body: Captivity did not still the elementals’ fury. Across their divided domains, the primordial powers wage endless war against one another.

sections.title: Breaching the Wards
sections.body:
Strong wards bar the way between Azeroth and the Elemental Plane, but they can break. Two centuries ago, near the desperate end of the War of the Three Hammers, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan pierced the veil and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord from the Firelands. His arrival ruptured the Redridge Mountains and forged Blackrock Mountain.

Now, volatile cracks have opened across Kalimdor. Dimensional rifts keep appearing in Silithus, Un'Goro Crater, Azshara, and Winterspring. Hostile elementals pour through and test the mortal world's defenses.

faq.answer: The Elemental Plane is where the titans imprisoned Azeroth’s chaotic elementals. Its four domains are Skywall for air, Deepholm for earth, the Abyssal Maw for water, and the Firelands for fire.

faq.q: Who created the Elemental Plane and why?
faq.answer: The titans created the Elemental Plane after defeating the Old Gods, whom the elemental lords had served. They banished the elementals there, and nature calmed across Azeroth’s surface.

faq.q: What are the four realms within the plane?
faq.answer: The four domains are Skywall for air, Deepholm for earth, the Abyssal Maw for water, and the Firelands for fire. Each belongs to one of the four primary elements.

faq.q: Can creatures travel between Azeroth and the Elemental Plane?
aliases: how to get to elemental plane
faq.answer: Ancient wards bar travel between Azeroth and the Elemental Plane, but powerful sorcery or unstable barriers can breach them. Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros across the veil, and volatile rifts now open at times in remote parts of Kalimdor.

faq.q: Why are elementals invading Kalimdor right now?
faq.answer: Rifts have opened across Silithus, Un'Goro Crater, Azshara, and Winterspring. They let waves of elementals from the Elemental Plane enter mortal lands, where defenders of the Horde and Alliance beat them back.

faq.q: How was Blackrock Mountain created by the plane?
faq.answer: During the War of the Three Hammers, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan tried to summon a fiery power to save his clan. He tore open a gateway to the Firelands and brought Ragnaros into Azeroth. The Firelord’s arrival shattered the surrounding mountains, carving out the Burning Steppes, Searing Gorge, and Blackrock Mountain.

angles.text: As a shaman, you seek harmony with spirits whose ancient rulers remain imprisoned beyond the veil. Knowing how Azeroth and the Elemental Plane are divided helps explain why summoned elements lash out.
As a mage, you draw on the distant realms’ fringe energies to conjure elemental familiars. Strict control keeps that magic from tearing wider breaches into the material world.
As a dwarf, you know the Dark Iron clan’s grim history warns what can happen when mortal ambition pierces the Elemental Plane to summon beings like Ragnaros.
As a Skyborne, you know Zephras Isle floats high within Skywall, a sanctuary in the Elemental Plane’s windy domain.
